rationale: NVIDIA announced an expanded Muse AI-agent collaboration (Vera Rubin GPUs, Spectrum-X networking, BlueField-4) alongside this investment, making NVIDIA both the allocator and the named compute/networking supplier for the Meta buildout this capital helps finance.

AMD co-invested as a Cornerstone Investor in the same Meta equity offering and separately holds warrants toward ~10% of Meta from its Feb 2026 chip-supply deal; the raise extends that GPU/compute supply relationship too.
Converting two Hong Kong colocation towers (iTech Tower 3.1/3.2) into Amazon capacity is a standard end-market for Vertiv's power and thermal-management equipment, though no specific vendor is named.
Electrical distribution and switchgear for fitting out these two towers is a typical Eaton order category for a colocation-to-hyperscale conversion, though not confirmed as the specific vendor.

General Intuition trains world/action models on large-scale gameplay video, a GPU-training-intensive workload; a $220M round at a $6.2B valuation funds further compute consumption on NVIDIA's platform.

The ~$40B master-lease financing explicitly covers Nvidia GPU pods and related equipment for SpaceX's AI compute buildout, per SpaceX's own Form 8-K and Apollo's press release; the financing exists to fund incremental NVIDIA GPU purchases.

NVIDIA's GPUs financed by this lease are fabricated by TSMC; a $40B commitment to expand SpaceX's GPU fleet is a second-order driver of TSMC's advanced-node wafer demand, consistent with TSM's already-converging beneficiary signal this week.
BlackRock is a named anchor investor in the same ~$40B master-lease financing that explicitly covers Nvidia GPU pods and related equipment for SpaceX's AI compute buildout.

Goldman Sachs is a named anchor investor and sole structuring agent on the same ~$40B master-lease financing that explicitly covers Nvidia GPU pods and related equipment for SpaceX's AI compute buildout.
KKR-advised capital accounts are a named anchor investor in the same ~$40B master-lease financing that explicitly covers Nvidia GPU pods and related equipment for SpaceX's AI compute buildout.
OpenAI's model training and inference run substantially on NVIDIA GPUs; SoftBank's final $10B tranche of its $30B follow-on commitment directly extends OpenAI's compute budget.
Microsoft is OpenAI's primary Azure compute partner and largest strategic shareholder; incremental OpenAI capital flows through Azure consumption commitments.
Oracle is a disclosed Stargate/OCI compute-capacity partner for OpenAI's buildout; additional OpenAI capital supports further Oracle cloud-capacity commitments.
Broadcom is OpenAI's disclosed custom-AI-accelerator (XPU) co-design partner; continued OpenAI funding supports that multi-year silicon program.

Several of the uprated Constellation plants (Dresden, LaSalle, Quad Cities, Limerick) are GE-designed boiling-water reactors; turbine and uprate services for this work are a natural order book for GE Vernova's nuclear-services business.

Reactor-internals, steam-generator and fuel-component work for nuclear uprates of this kind is core to BWX Technologies' nuclear-services business, though no specific vendor is named for this program.
~1.1GW of added nuclear capacity implies incremental enrichment demand over the plants' operating life -- a thematic, second-order read on Centrus Energy's enrichment business.

Constellation's own release ties most of the added capacity to a 20-year PPA with Google, locking in carbon-free baseload power for Google's AI-datacenter buildout -- an offtake benefit, not a supply one.
Constellation's own release names Amazon alongside Google as a 20-year PPA offtaker for the added nuclear capacity, securing carbon-free power for Amazon's AI-datacenter buildout.
1.6GW of new gas-fired generation funded by this loan is a natural gas-turbine order book for GE Vernova, the leading domestic gas-turbine OEM, though no vendor is named.
The ~1GW of battery storage funded by this loan is a direct product-market fit for Fluence Energy's grid-scale storage integration business.
DOE's own framing of this loan as strengthening the grid implies switchgear/distribution equipment spend, a typical Eaton order category, though no vendor is named.
